library.conLosNumerosSon: {value} with {championName}: the numbers are a snapshot, not a verdict. Keep logging; with 10+ matches the analysis gets much more accurate.
library.conTenesUnoDe: With {championName} you have one of your most solid profiles: {numericWr}% WR over {totalGames} matches and a {value} KDA. At this sample size those numbers aren't noise: you're doing something right consistently. The next step isn't playing safer, it's figuring out what you do in lost matches that breaks that pattern.
library.ganasConPeroTu: You win with {championName}, but your KDA ({value}) suggests it isn't through individual dominance. Your value is probably in macro: objectives, map pressure, showing up for key fights. That's hard to see in the numbers, and sometimes it's exactly right. Even so, lowering your average deaths ({deathsAvg} per match) should push your winrate even higher.
library.hayUnaContradiccionInteresante: There's an interesting contradiction with {championName}: your KDA is {value}, but your winrate is {numericWr}%. You're playing well individually, but that edge isn't turning into wins. Ask yourself whether you're closing out games when you're ahead, or prioritizing farm/kills over decisive objectives like Baron or the inhibitor.
library.tuRolConEs: Your role with {championName} is clearly an enabler: {value} average assists against {value2} kills says your impact lives in your teammates' plays. That's not bad, it's a style. The key question is whether that impact holds when your team doesn't turn your plays into kills, because that's where utility champions lose value.
library.conJugasParaKills: With {championName} you play for kills: {value} per match and relatively few assists. That can be a strength if your damage takes out key threats, but it can also mean you're picking solo skirmishes when the team needs something more collective. Check whether your fights line up with map objectives.
library.sosConsistenteConEn: You're consistent with {championName}: in {value}% of your matches you finish with 3 deaths or fewer. The problem isn't survival, it's impact: you don't die, but you don't decide games either. Look to be more aggressive at key moments: take Baron fights, force inhibitors when ahead, call rotations.
library.hayUnaTendenciaClara: There's a clear improvement trend with {championName}: your overall WR is {numericWr}%, but over your last {recentMatchesCount} matches it went up to {value}%. You did something differently, whether in builds, map decisions or matchups you understood better. It's worth figuring out what changed so you don't lose it.
library.tuWrHistoricoCon: Your all-time WR with {championName} is {numericWr}%, but over the last {recentMatchesCount} matches it dropped to {value}%. It could be a meta shift, climbing in MMR or just variance. Before forcing more games, check whether something concrete changed, in the patch, your habits or the matchups you're facing.
library.elDatoMasUrgente: The most urgent stat with {championName} is deaths: {deathsAvg} per match on average is high for any role. Every extra death isn't just a respawn, it's gold given away, a lost objective and ceded map pressure. Cutting down to {value} average deaths would probably have a direct impact on your winrate.
library.estaEnUnBuen: {championName} is in a good spot in the meta (tier score {value}), but your personal winrate ({numericWr}%) doesn't show it. The champion may be strong in the hands of players with a specific style that isn't yours yet. Watch how top ladder players play it: there may be something specific in builds or play patterns you're not applying.
library.estasSacandoDeWr: You're getting {numericWr}% WR with {championName} even though the meta doesn't favor it (tier score {value}). That shows real mastery: you know when it works and when it doesn't. The risk is when the meta hurts it more actively; keep watching whether the results hold up with the patch.
library.inicioPrometedorConEn: Promising start with {championName}: {numericWr}% over {totalGames} matches. It's still too small a sample to be conclusive, but the direction is good. Once you hit 15–20 matches you'll have a much clearer picture of whether it's a pick that helps you or just a good start.
library.tuPerfilConEsta: Your profile with {championName} is balanced: {numericWr}% WR, {value} KDA, {deathsAvg} average deaths. There's no red flag, but no clear dominance either. Your most likely room for improvement is cutting deaths in lost games and forcing more objectives when you're ahead.

legal.about:
Rift Deck was born from a simple idea: help players better understand the game they enjoy.

We believe improving isn't only about reflexes or mechanics. Every match produces valuable information: decisions, patterns, mistakes, wins and learning opportunities. Our goal is to turn that data into useful tools so any player can analyze their performance, optimize their choices and make smarter decisions on the Rift.

The platform brings together stats, builds, match analysis, performance tracking, champion, item and rune information, and strategy tools designed for both casual and competitive players.

Rift Deck is an independent project developed and maintained by {owner}.

## Plans and payments

Rift Deck is currently free and doesn't charge any subscription. If paid plans are offered in the future, their prices and conditions will be published before you can sign up for them, as described in the Terms and conditions.

## Contact

You can write to us at **{email}**.

laneSurvival.top: In top, when the enemy jungler isn't showing on the map, don't push past the river: let the wave come to you and save your escape for the gank.
laneSurvival.jungler: In the jungle, don't invade or contest an objective without lane priority: if your mid or bot can't move first, give up that camp and take the one on the other side of the map.
laneSurvival.mid: In mid, don't step into the river or the enemy jungle without knowing where their jungler is; if you can't see them, push the wave and back off before roaming.
laneSurvival.adc: As a marksman, hit whatever is closest and never be the first one in: stay behind your frontline and save Flash to escape, not to chase.
laneSurvival.support: As a support, don't go warding alone ahead of your team: do it with lane priority or with company, and don't engage if your marksman can't follow.
laneSurvival.any: Before every fight, count how many enemies you can see on the map: if two or more are missing, don't go in first or drift away from your team.
laneSurvival.supportEnchanter: As a support, stay behind your marksman and don't go warding alone: save your shields and heals for when the enemy goes in, not for lane trades.

isolatedAction.top: When the first dragon or Herald spawns, use the window to rotate: push your wave and move to the river before the fight starts, not after.
isolatedAction.jungler: After each camp, check which lane has priority and gank there; being at dragon and Herald fights matters more than full-clearing.
isolatedAction.mid: Every time you push your wave, move to the nearest lane or objective: mid is the lane that reaches fights fastest.
isolatedAction.adc: Group with your support and your team for objectives: a marksman farming alone while the team fights loses the game even with the gold.
isolatedAction.support: Go with your jungler to objectives and roam mid when your marksman is safe: a support who is in every fight multiplies the team.
isolatedAction.any: When your team groups for an objective, arrive before the fight starts: push your wave and move early.

healing.title: You're missing anti-heal against teams that heal
healing.timing: Build it as your 2nd item as soon as you see 2 healers in draft; in fights, hold your damage until the healer uses their ability.
healing.timingTank: Build it as your 2nd or 3rd item as soon as you see 2 healers in draft and stay in front during fights: the anti-heal applies to whoever hits you.
healing.timingSupport: Build it as your 2nd or 3rd item as soon as you see 2 healers, and get your marksman to bring anti-heal too: together you cut their healing.

magic.title: You're not defending against magic damage
magic.timing: Make it your 2nd or 3rd item and don't line up with their mages: wait for them to use their abilities before going in.
magic.timingCarry: As a carry, don't trade damage for a tank item: pick a damage item with magic resist or a shield as your 4th or 5th item when their mages are bursting you, and wait for them to use their abilities before going in.
magic.timingTank: Make it your 2nd or 3rd item: with magic resist you can go in first and soak their abilities so your carries fight freely.
magic.timingSupport: Get magic resist from a support item that also protects your team, and don't walk ahead to ward while their mages are out of sight.

physical.title: You're not defending against physical damage
physical.timing: Make it your 2nd or 3rd item; against marksmen and fighters, armor is worth more than health alone.
physical.timingCarry: As a carry, don't trade damage for a tank item: pick a damage item that also defends as your 4th or 5th item when enemy physical damage is shredding you, and stay behind your frontline.
physical.timingTank: Make it your 2nd or 3rd item: against marksmen and fighters, armor is worth more than raw health, and it lets you take the first burst so your team can answer.
physical.timingSupport: Get armor from a support item that also protects your team, and in fights look after your marksman instead of chasing damage.

cc.title: Enemy crowd control catches you without tenacity
cc.present: several champions with hard CC who start fights, look for picks or dive you
cc.timing: Get it with your boots or as your 3rd item, and don't go in first: let them waste their CC on your frontline.
cc.timingCarry: Get tenacity from your boots or a damage item with a CC cleanse, and don’t go in until they waste their CC on your frontline.
cc.timingTank: Get it with your boots or as your 3rd item: as the frontline, go in first so they waste their CC on you and your carries fight freely.
cc.timingSupport: Get tenacity from your boots; if their CC lands on your marksman, an item that cleanses your ally saves them more than your own tenacity.
cc.timingEnchanter: You don't need tenacity yourself: if their CC lands on your marksman, build an item that cleanses your ally and save it for the moment they get caught.

burst.title: Assassins delete you without an anti-burst item
burst.present: 2 or more assassins or burst champions
burst.timing: Build it when the enemy assassin gets ahead and save its active for the moment they jump on you.
burst.timingCarry: Build it after your core damage items when the enemy assassin gets ahead, and save its effect for the moment they jump on you.
burst.timingSupport: Build it when the enemy assassin gets ahead: an item that shields your team saves your marksman as well as you.

tanks.title: You're missing penetration against tank teams
tanks.timing: Build it as your 3rd item: before that, your damage still works against their base resistances.

shields.title: Enemy shields are eating your damage
shields.timing: Build it when shields are winning your trades; in fights, punish after the shield is gone.
